paper.title: Sequential Learning of the Pareto Front for Multi-objective Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Pareto set identification in multi-objective multi-armed bandits (fixed confidence)
unmapped: goal is to identify the Pareto set of arm means with probability >= 1-delta (delta-PAC), minimizing expected stopping time
Gaussian rewards with identity covariance (independent objectives)
settings.definition_quote:
given $K$ independent probability distributions on $\R^d$, $
u = (
u_k)_{k \in [K]} \in V$, with respective means $\mu$... at every time step $t$ an agent gets to pick an arm $A_t \in [K]$ and receives an independent reward $X_t \in \R^d$ drawn from $
u_{A_t}$... we are interested in identifying all the Pareto optimal arms.

algorithms.name: Track-and-Stop for Pareto front identification (with efficient minimal transportation cost oracle)

cited_results.cited_title: Optimal best arm identification with fixed confidence
cited_results.setting_description: Fixed-confidence active sequential hypothesis testing in bandits (applies to Pareto set identification): any delta-PAC strategy; T_star(nu)^{-1} = sup_w inf_{lambda in Alt(nu)} sum_k w_k KL(nu_k, lambda_k)
